newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgians lose faith in institutions - poll.
newsitem.headline: Belgians lose faith in institutions - poll.

text.p: Belgian have lost faith in their country's institutions following a spate of scandals, a newspaper poll published on Thursday showed.
Of 2,000 Belgians polled by daily La Libre Belgique, 83 percent said the country's institutions functioned badly and 64 percent said they believed democracy in Belgium was in danger.
Belgium has been in a prolongued crisis since mid-August, when police discovered a paedophile kidnap, sex and murder ring which has claimed the lives of at least four girls.
A parliamentary inquiry into the way police and the judiciary handled the investigation of the paedophile ring has revealed a catalogue of blunders.

The country has also been rocked by a series of arrests in relation to the 1991 Mafia-style murder of socialist politician Andre Cools, by a court investigation into child sex allegations against two ministers and by a long string of financial scandals involving politicians.

Belgians expect no salvation from the world of politics, the poll showed: 77 percent of the people polled said they thought the political world was not able to reform the justice system and other levels of government administration.
However, the state of affairs in neighbouring countries is not considered much better as 54 percent said Belgium is not faring worse than France, Germany, the Netherlands or Britain.
